reason: Confirmed with caveats. The old R28-A4 (iv) test 'daily|allowance|submission limit|limit' is inserted before R27N-4's HARD FAIL line. R27N-4 has no network 'continue' step before it, so any submit output containing 'limit' returns 3 = STOP. Overstatement: every real 429 in the session transcripts has the raise_for_status form '429 Client Error: Too Many Requests for url: ...', which contains no 'limit', so the old regex would NOT stop on it. The limits-endpoint call after a submit is wrapped in try/except in kaggle 2.2.4 (kaggle_api_extended.py l.2025-2035), so a 429 on GetSubmissionLimits never reaches the output either. The real defect is a JSON-body error (kagglesdk kaggle_http_client.py l.130: HTTPError(resp['message'])) whose text says 'rate limit' or similar. Tested: 'Rate limit exceeded.' -> old DAILY (exit 3), v3 NETWORK. The v3 order (success -> network incl. 429/Too Many/rate.?limit/Max retries/rc 124 -> daily without a bare 'limit' -> hard fail -> UNKNOWN = list first) classifies all 8 samples correctly. Samples: the classic 'daily Submission allowance ... tomorrow' -> DAILY; DNS 'Max retries exceeded' -> NETWORK, so 'exceeded' is safe only because of the order; 'does not exist' -> HARD; '0 submissions remaining today.' -> SUCCESS. Feasibility: it is text only, already in night_checklist.md section P, and has no effect on the model or its output. Duplicate-safe because nb_try lists first. It fits R1-R10 and the schedule. Value: operational only (no score, no private effect). G2's used_today gate makes a genuine night daily-limit answer near-unreachable, so the fix mainly removes one mis-classification path that would stop the batch.
fix: Keep nb_try v3 exactly as written in research/wf_ideas_v4/round29/night_checklist.md l.35-48; never re-add a bare 'limit' and never move the daily test above the network test. Optional one-token hardening (not required): add 'maximum number of submissions' to the daily regex; today that text falls to UNKNOWN, which is harmless (list-first retries, then GAVE UP -> section N). Correct the evidence wording in the freeze/CONTEXT line: the observed 429 form ('429 Client Error: Too Many Requests') would not have tripped the old regex; the risk is a JSON 'rate limit' message.
realistic_gain: 0 LB points. It cuts a small (<1-2%) chance that the night batch STOPs wrongly on a JSON 'rate limit' answer with the user asleep. That event would cost up to 3 night reads (stack, exp75, exp89p) and push them into LATE.
